```{r setup, include = F}

gc()

hfwgtex::hfwg_use(overwrite = T)

library(scf)
library(scales)
library(ggplot2)

```

```{r lede calcs, include = F}

for (i in seq(1989, 2022, 3)){
  
  data <- scf_load(i)
  data0 <- data
  
  data <- scf_subset(data, x8023 %in% c(1,2))
  
  data <- scf_update(data,
                     p1_sex = x8021,
                     p2_sex = x103,
                     race1 = x6809,
                     race2 = x6810)
 
  # NOTE: Race variable appears to have changed over time.
  # Next step is this
  
  # Subset Mixed Sex for Calculation Purposes
  data <- scf_update(data,
                     same_sex = p1_sex == p2_sex)
  
  samesex <- scf_freq(data, ~same_sex)$results$proportion[2]
  assign(paste0("samesex_", i), samesex)
  
  data1 <- data
  data <- scf_subset(data, same_sex == FALSE)
   
  data <- scf_update(data,
                     race_male = ifelse(p1_sex == 1, race1,
                                        ifelse(p2_sex == 1, race2, NA)),
                     race_female = ifelse(p1_sex == 2, race1,
                                          ifelse(p2_sex == 2), race2, NA))
  
  data <- scf_update(data,
                     exogamous = race_male != race_female)

  
}


```



# Context

America has a long history of racial segregation and conflict. It has also wrestled with a long-term effort to achieve racial integration.  Part of this has been the legalization and social acceptance of interracial marriage.  How much progress has occurred on this front?

The incidence of interracial unions is one useful indicator of the degree to which racial integration has progressed.  It is difficult to imagine a more fundamental or socially consequential form of racial integration than in pairing choices. The choice of pairing with someone has wide-ranging consequences, and the choice to pair across racial boundaries is a clear revealed preference for deprioritizing racial identity as a relevant criterion for mate selection. When such unions produce offspring, they contribute a new generation of Americans with mixed racial heritage, for whom there is little benefit and much threat to conflicts among racial purists.

Opinions differ on the progress of this social project.  This analysis capitalizes on the *Survey of Consumer Finances*, a high-quality national survey whose data includes information on individual household members' races. While racial integration is far more complicated than the incidence of interracial marriage, the analysis offers a data-derived sense of its general progress and trajectory.
